arxiv-2204-11146.title: Gabor is Enough: Interpretable Deep Denoising with a Gabor Synthesis Dictionary Prior
arxiv-2204-11146.creator: Nikola Janjušević, Amirhossein Khalilian-Gourtani, and Yao Wang
arxiv-2204-11146.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Nikola Janjušević, Amirhossein Khalilian-Gourtani, and Yao Wang. Image processing neural networks, natural and artificial, have a long history with orientation-selectivity, often described mathematically as Gabor filters. Gabor-like filters have been observed in the early layers of CNN classifiers and even throughout low-level image processing networks. In this work, we take this observation to the extreme and explicitly constrain the filters of a natural-image denoising CNN to be learned 2D real Gabor filters.

arxiv-2305-06289.title: Learning Video-Conditioned Policies for Unseen Manipulation Tasks
arxiv-2305-06289.creator: Elliot Chane-Sane, Cordelia Schmid, Ivan Laptev
arxiv-2305-06289.description: Abstract The ability to specify robot commands by a non-expert user is critical for building generalist agents capable of solving a large variety of tasks. One convenient way to specify the intended robot goal is by a video of a person demonstrating the target task.

arxiv-2309-06735.title: GelFlow: Self-supervised Learning of Optical Flow for Vision-Based Tactile Sensor Displacement Measurement
arxiv-2309-06735.creator: Zhiyuan Zhang, Hua Yang, Zhouping Yin
arxiv-2309-06735.description: Abstract High-resolution multi-modality information acquired by vision-based tactile sensors can support more dexterous manipulations for robot fingers. Optical flow is low-level information directly obtained by vision-based tactile sensors, which can be transformed into other modalities like force, geometry and depth. Current vision-tactile sensors employ optical flow methods from OpenCV to estimate the deformation of markers in gels.

arxiv-2311-00213.title: Consistent Video-to-Video Transfer Using Synthetic Dataset
arxiv-2311-00213.creator: Jiaxin Cheng, Tianjun Xiao & Tong He
arxiv-2311-00213.description: Abstract We introduce a novel and efficient approach for text-based video-to-video editing that eliminates the need for resource-intensive per-video-per-model finetuning. At the core of our approach is a synthetic paired video dataset tailored for video-to-video transfer tasks. Inspired by Instruct Pix2Pix’s image transfer via editing instruction, we adapt this paradigm to the video domain.

arxiv-2311-03920.title: An Intelligent Edge-Deployable Indoor Air Quality Monitoring and Activity Recognition Approach
arxiv-2311-03920.creator: Mohamed Rafik Aymene Berkani 1 , Ammar Chouchane 2,4 , Yassine Himeur 3 , Abdelmalik Ouamane 4 and Abbes Amira 5
arxiv-2311-03920.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mohamed Rafik Aymene Berkani 1 , Ammar Chouchane 2,4 , Yassine Himeur 3 , Abdelmalik Ouamane 4 and Abbes Amira 5. The surveillance of indoor air quality is paramount for ensuring environmental safety, a task made increasingly viable due to advancements in technology and the application of artificial intelligence and deep learning (DL) tools. This paper introduces an intelligent system dedicated to monitoring air quality and categorizing activities within indoor environments using a DL approach based on 1D Convolutional Neural Networks (1D-CNNs).

arxiv-2402-18141.title: Urysohn 1-width for 4 and 5 manifolds with positive biRicci curvature
arxiv-2402-18141.creator: Junyu Ma
arxiv-2402-18141.description: Abstract . In this paper, we show that closed four and five manifolds with positive biRicci curvature have finite Urysohn 1-width bounded by a constant that depends on the curvature bounds. During the proof, we can also observe that the fundamental group of those manifolds is virtually free.

arxiv-2410-09223.title: The Same but Different: Structural Similarities and Differences in Multilingual Language Modeling
arxiv-2410-09223.creator: Ruochen Zhang, Qinan Yu, Matianyu Zang, Carsten Eickhoff, Ellie Pavlick
arxiv-2410-09223.description: Abstract We employ new tools from mechanistic interpretability in order to ask whether the internal structure of large language models (LLMs) shows correspondence to the linguistic structures which underlie the languages on which they are trained. In particular, we ask (1) when two languages employ the same morphosyntactic processes, do LLMs handle them using shared internal circuitry?

arxiv-2410-24226.title: Tensegrity Robot Proprioceptive State Estimation with Geometric Constraints
arxiv-2410-24226.creator: Wenzhe Tong, Tzu-Yuan Lin, Jonathan Mi, Yicheng Jiang, Maani Ghaffari, Xiaonan Huang
arxiv-2410-24226.description: Abstract Tensegrity robots, characterized by a synergistic assembly of rigid rods and elastic cables, form robust structures that are resistant to impacts. However, this design introduces complexities in kinematics and dynamics, complicating control and state estimation. This work presents a novel proprioceptive state estimator for tensegrity robots.

arxiv-2501-04018.title: MERCURY: A fast and versatile multi-resolution based global emulator of compound climate hazards
arxiv-2501-04018.creator: Shruti Nath, Julie Carreau, Kai Kornhuber, Peter Pfleiderer, Carl-Friedrich Schleussner, Philippe Naveau
arxiv-2501-04018.description: Abstract High-impact climate damages are often driven by compounding climate conditions. For example, elevated heat stress conditions can arise from a combination of high humidity and temperature. To explore future changes in compounding hazards under a range of climate scenarios and with large ensembles, climate emulators can provide light-weight, data-driven complements to Earth System Models.

arxiv-2503-08984.title: Phase Transitions in Planted k k -Factor Recovery
arxiv-2503-08984.creator: Julia Gaudio, Colin Sandon, Jiaming Xu, Dana Yang
arxiv-2503-08984.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Julia Gaudio, Colin Sandon, Jiaming Xu, Dana Yang. This paper studies the problem of inferring a k k -factor, specifically a spanning k k -regular graph, planted within an Erdős–Rényi random graph 𝒢 ⁡ ( n , λ / n ) {\mathcal{G}}(n,\lambda/n) . We show that as the average degree λ \lambda surpasses the critical threshold of 1 / k 1/k , the inference problem undergoes a transition from almost exact recovery to partial recovery.

arxiv-2503-22553.title: Tracing the Heliospheric Magnetic Field via Anisotropic Radio-Wave Scattering
arxiv-2503-22553.creator: Daniel L. Clarkson, Eduard P. Kontar, Nicolina Chrysaphi, A. Gordon Emslie, Natasha L. S. Jeffrey, Vratislav Krupar, Antonio Vecchio
arxiv-2503-22553.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniel L. Clarkson, Eduard P. Kontar, Nicolina Chrysaphi, A. Gordon Emslie, Natasha L. S. Jeffrey, Vratislav Krupar, Antonio Vecchio. Astrophysical radio sources are embedded in turbulent magnetised environments. In the 1 MHz sky, solar radio bursts are the brightest sources, produced by electrons travelling along magnetic field lines from the Sun through the heliosphere. We demonstrate that the magnetic field not only guides the emitting electrons, but also directs radio waves via anisotropic scattering from density irregularities in the magnetised plasma.

pmc-11075033.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). pmc-12442832.title: Changes in monocyte subsets are associated with an increased risk of AAA and are surrogate markers for AAA morphology in patients with late-stage disease
pmc-12442832.creator: Bianca Hamann, Anna Klimova, Marvin Kapalla, David M. Poitz, Albert Busch, Henning Morawietz, Christian Reeps, Anja Hofmann
pmc-12442832.description: IntroductionMonocytes play a role in the pathology of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and can display immunophenotypic heterogeneity. Alterations in monocyte subsets are associated with cardiovascular risk, but their profile in AAA is poorly understood.AimWe aimed to comprehensively define associations of monocyte phenotypes with AAA risk and AAA morphology.

pmc-12612277.title: Continuous tuning of ejector parameters via zeotropic component migration for optimising high-temperature heat pump
pmc-12612277.creator: Zhengyong Li, Youcai Liang, Yan Zhu, Shunchun Yao, Zhibin Yu
pmc-12612277.description: As the temperature lift increases, heat pump performance declines due to rising throttling losses in expansion valves. Ejectors present a promising alternative, enabling power recovery from the throttling process. However, fixed-geometry ejectors suffer performance degradation under off-design conditions. Here we propose leveraging the component migration characteristics of zeotropic refrigerants to continuously adjust critical ejector parameters by modulating the quality.

pmc-12617111.title: ΟΑ2063. Facilitators & Barriers to occupant restraint system use in the Eastern Med Reg: A scoping review
pmc-12617111.creator: F M Shebbo, F Vaca, H Mowafi, M Price, S Zaytoun, M Kabalan, A Bracket, L Ghandour, S Al-Hajj
pmc-12617111.description: BackgroundRoad traffic injury is a public health concern preventable by occupant restraint systems (ORS), i.e., child car seats and seatbelts. In the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR), road injuries are high while ORS use is low. This scoping review aims to identify facilitators/barriers, map and describe intervention studies improving ORS use in the EMR.

pmc-12638237.title: Assessing the Impact of BMI and Glycaemic Control on Cardiac Autonomic Neuropathy in Patients with Early and Long-standing Diabetes Mellitus: A Window of Opportunity
pmc-12638237.creator: Mamta Shobhawat, Shival Srivastav, Ravindra Gayaprasad Shukla, Om Lata Bhagat
pmc-12638237.description: BackgroundCardiac autonomic neuropathy (CAN) is a well-known, yet underreported, complication of Diabetes mellitus (DM). CAN assessment can be performed using heart rate variability (HRV) and Ewing’s battery of tests. Severity of CAN may be affected by multiple factors like glycaemic control, obesity and co-existing distal neuropathy. However, the relationship between CAN and these factors remains underexplored.
